Nobody checks the plan before it reaches you. So I had to build the checks. That's the uncomfortable bit about generated training plans and most companies won't say it out loud. Hard rules it simply cannot break: no heavy squats and deadlifts back to back, no max attempt in week one, no high-rep olympic lifting under fatigue, no skill progression you haven't earned. Different rules per sport, because people get hurt differently.

I added friction on purpose, and I'd do it again. Coaches and physios build plans for other people - that's a different responsibility to building one for yourself. So the professional route asks for credentials before you can build for anyone, requires you to accept a disclaimer, and needs your approval on every plan before it reaches a client. Fewer signups. Better ones. Clinical judgement never leaves the professional.

What happens when the plan is wrong? Every company avoids this question. Here's ours: you've got 48 hours, or until your first logged session, to tell us what's wrong. We fix it. No charge, no argument. After that it's fixed - because by then you're training, not correcting. Small window on purpose. Long enough for a mistake, short enough that one payment isn't an unlimited rewrite.
